_comment: PROMOTION REGISTRY for harness/tests/'s fast tier (round 385, harness A). Read by harness/tierbudget.py, which harness/tests/conftest.py consults when it applies the `swe_slow` marker. Round 235's filename rule still decides the DEFAULT and still decides it alone: a `test_swe_*.py` file ABSENT from `promoted` is slow, so a new file tiers itself with no edit here -- round 235's self-maintenance property, kept. This file can only ever move a file toward the tier a human is watching, and only on a measurement. A stale entry costs wall-clock; it cannot cost coverage. Two bars for an entry: MEASURED under `cap_s` by `tierbudget.py measure` (each file alone, fresh process, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1), and GREEN when measured -- a red file is never promotable however cheap, because the fast tier is what the driver's per-round health check reports and a promotion must not turn every future round's line red for a defect it did not cause. Every promoted file is re-timed FOR FREE by the fast-tier run itself (conftest.py's pytest_terminal_summary hook), which prints a `tier-budget:` line above pytest's count line and says DRIFT when a file outgrows max(measured_s * drift_factor, measured_s + drift_floor_s). Do not hand-edit a `measured_s`: re-run the ladder and re-decide.

test_swe_coverage.py.why: coverage instrumentation over the whence tree; round 217 measured it with test_swe_triage.py at 150.4s for the pair, which is 28x its cost today

test_swe_mutation.py.why: the most expensive promotion and the one most likely to drift; kept because the cap is the policy and an unmeasured exemption is the thing this round removed. RE-MEASURED by round 485 (SWE-loop D) after adding nine id-stability tests: 18.17s -> 20.63s SOLO, still under the 25s cap and green, so the promotion stands on a measurement rather than on inertia. The `n_tests` this replaces (15) had been stale since round 385 -- the file collected 24 at round 479 and 33 now; nothing reads that field, which is why it drifted. A first run this round reported 27.3s while a pristine-worktree baseline was running on this 1-CPU box: that is a CONTENDED number and is not the one recorded here.

test_swe_oracles.py.why: holds all three injected-bug tests (fast_slow / direct / frames) — round 383 item 5's actual ask; these are the tests that go red on a language change and the whole reason the tier was re-measured

test_swe_prioritize.py.why: was NEVER measured (`unknown` in the slow-tier ledger) and was 60% red on this host until round 385 fixed campaign._dump_json's shared temp name; promoted so the fix cannot silently regress

test_swe_proc.py.why: process helpers; reads the whence corpus (15k reads) but does almost no interpreting

test_swe_scoreaudit.py.why: pure arithmetic over recorded campaign data, no interpreter reads at all

test_swe_triage.py.why: mutation triage over JSON; no interpreter reads at all

test_swe_depthceiling.py.why: round 389's ceiling tests: they pin the FRAME_SLACK derivation, the undercharge detection band and render's pair-coverage line, all of which go red on a language-constant change (FAST_MAX_DEPTH, MAX_NESTING, DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH) -- exactly the class round 383 found hiding in the slow tier for 15 rounds

test_swe_toolliveness.py.measured_by: python3 -m pytest tests/test_swe_toolliveness.py -q (fresh process, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, twice: 1.76s / 1.65s)
test_swe_toolliveness.py.why: the per-commit liveness sweep. 20 of its 21 tests run against a CONSTRUCTED git history in a tempdir, so it is cheap and has no dependence on this repo's own state; the 3 that pin the historical claim skip when their shas are unreachable. Promoted because the thing it guards -- can bench/ref_diff.py actually run -- went undetected for 5 rounds, and a guard in the slow tier is a guard nobody runs (round 390's item 3: four slow-tier runs in thirty rounds).

test_swe_instrument.py.why: the shared instrument-digest guard (round 389's item 4, finished round 401). Pure hashing and dict arithmetic -- no interpreter reads at all, 0.57s. Promoted because the thing it guards is a SILENT failure: a sweep that spans an edit to its own generator reports numbers that look like results, and round 389's single-hash version could not see a generator edit at all. A guard in the slow tier is a guard nobody runs (round 390's item 3).

test_swe_spacewitness.py.why: round 401's tightening of the tail-transparency SPACE exemption. Holds the only tests that pin the tightened branch, the map/oracle agreement on T-SPACE and the self-verifying anchor that follows it -- all of which go red on a change to oracles.py's tail branch or to Interpreter.DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH, the same class round 383 found hiding in the slow tier for 15 rounds.

test_swe_abconfound.py.why: ab()'s comparability guard: pure JSONL-in/dict-out over synthetic rows plus four committed sweep arms, no interpreter reads at all. Promoted for the same reason as test_swe_instrument.py above -- what it guards is a SILENT failure, and a guard in the slow tier is a guard nobody runs

test_swe_copyparity_real_subject.py.why: points copyparity at the REAL subject (languages/whence) instead of a tmp_path toy: the static `escapes` scan plus the `collect` differential. Belongs in the fast tier BECAUSE it is fail-closed -- a new file under languages/whence that resolves a path outside itself must go red in the round that writes it, which is the round that can still cheaply fix it, not weeks later in a mutation baseline gate. The expensive `run` mode (283 s) is deliberately NOT in this file.
